intro: Good end of life care keeps a person comfortable, safe and dignified, delivered by a team you support within your role.
points: Comfort and dignity guide everything — keep the person clean, warm and calm, and treat them exactly as they wish.
You support comfort and escalate; you never diagnose, change medicines or make treatment decisions — report symptoms to a nurse promptly.
A DNACPR decision relates only to CPR, so comfort, pain relief, food, fluids and kindness all continue as before.
Hearing is often the last sense to fade, so keep speaking gently and tell the dying person what you are doing.
Do not force food or fluids near the end of life; offer sips for comfort and give frequent mouth care.
Watch for pain in those who cannot speak, such as a furrowed brow, and respect cultural and religious wishes.
